key_insight: MonoIR-RS shows that infrared remote-sensing data can support effective vision-language learning when datasets and models are adapted beyond visible-band assumptions. The paper creates a new benchmark and uses CLIP-style and VLM adaptation to improve infrared understanding.
problem_solved: Most existing remote-sensing vision-language datasets and models are built around RGB/visible imagery, leaving infrared remote-sensing semantics underexplored. This paper addresses the lack of large-scale IR vision-language resources and methods tailored to IR-specific cues like object-background contrast and illumination invariance.
method: Builds MonoIR-RS, a large-scale infrared remote-sensing vision-language dataset and benchmark.
Constructs IR-aware training data to better reflect infrared scene characteristics and semantics.
Adapts CLIP-style contrastive learning and VLM components for infrared image-language alignment.
impact: This work gives practitioners a new benchmark for evaluating infrared vision-language systems and a stronger foundation for building models that work in non-visible sensing conditions. It is especially useful for remote sensing, surveillance, and multimodal AI applications where RGB-only methods are insufficient.

paper_title: MonoIR-RS: Infrared Remote Sensing Vision-Language Learning with CLIP and VLM Adaptation
paper_authors: Jiaju Han, Ma Yaqi, Yahui Chai, Xuemeng Sun, Xin Li
